text:
oliver: hey team — first week setup trouble. I'm on an M1 Mac using Colima. When I run `docker compose up` the redis container exits immediately with a PermissionError trying to bind to a unix socket at /data/redis.sock. Postgres complains about volume permissions too. Also tried mounting /var/run/docker.sock into a helper container and get permission denied. any quick tips?

alex: are you on Colima or Docker Desktop? Colima keeps its socket under ~/.colima by default, so mounting /var/run/docker.sock from mac host won't behave the same as linux. what does `colima status` say?

maria: common pattern — either run redis as the same uid that owns the host dir, or chown the host dir before starting. add `user: "1000"` to the redis service in compose or ensure the host mount directory exists and is writable. example snippet: 
```
services:
  redis:
    image: redis:6
    volumes:
      - ./tmp/redis:/data
    user: "1000"
    command: redis-server --unixsocket /data/redis.sock --unixsocketperm 700
```

alex: for Colima mounts you often need to start it with mounts enabled: `colima stop && colima start --mount`. also run on host: `mkdir -p ./tmp/redis && sudo chown $UID:$GID ./tmp/redis` so the container user can write.

devx: quick note about docker.sock on mac: you can use the colima socket instead of trying to mount mac's /var/run/docker.sock. either `-v $HOME/.colima/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock` in compose or `export DOCKER_HOST=unix://$HOME/.colima/docker.sock` when running docker commands locally. Docker Desktop manages the socket differently and chowning it isn't possible.

oliver: OK I ran `colima stop && colima start --mount`, created ./tmp/redis and `sudo chown $UID:$GID ./tmp/redis`, and added `user: "1000"` to the redis service. after that redis and postgres started fine. for the docker.sock case I'll point tools at `~/.colima/docker.sock` for now. thanks everyone :tada:

infra-bot: If this keeps recurring for other new hires, please add a short note to the onboarding docs (./docs/local-setup.md) and tag #devex so we can track it.

maria: going to add a brief section to onboarding notes with the exact commands mentioned here. :thumbsup:
